evidence_status: public management/research need; not ATLAS customer demand or validation

records.empirical_evidence: Houston’s FY2026–2030 CIP estimates $1.156 billion for storm-drainage improvements, with about $170 million for Local Drainage Program and Storm Water Action Team projects. The plan describes objective ranking of flood-protection needs and design for 2-year collection-system rainfall while reducing structural-flood risk during 100-year events.
records.validation_path: Overlay only city-published drainage project and channel/detention geodata available for the 25 km study box; compare event-period satellite classifications with city/USGS gauge records and dated official flood reports. Record geometry/date coverage before analysis.
records.scope_limit: CIP allocations are planned estimates, not measured reductions in flood loss; the plan cautions that receiving-system capacity can still cause flooding.

records.empirical_evidence: NOAA NCCOS reports a rainfall-flood model demonstrated over roughly 1,000 km² of Miami-Dade using rain, gauges, topography, land use, flood infrastructure, and groundwater. For a four-day May 2020 Memorial Day flood period, canal water levels were predicted with about 15 cm average accuracy and the model ran at least 30 times faster than real time.
records.validation_path: Use documented gauge/canal levels, rainfall timing, and independently mapped event reports for a held-out event; treat the NOAA 2020 experiment as contextual precedent, not as ATLAS ground truth or performance evidence.
records.scope_limit: The NOAA demonstration is county-scale and predates the current candidate window; it does not validate the 625 km² candidate box or ATLAS.

records.empirical_evidence: USGS deployed eight wave sensors between Naples and Crystal River to measure Hurricane Milton coastal impacts and added a rapid deployment gauge in St. Petersburg; USGS also documented post-storm flood measurements and gauge repairs along Florida’s Gulf Coast.
records.validation_path: Match any candidate-box OPERA dates to USGS/NWS gauge time series and geolocated high-water marks or official event reports. Keep regional instruments outside the box as context and do not count them as local reference samples.
records.scope_limit: The cited sensors cover a regional coast and do not establish adequate independent labels inside the Tampa candidate box.

records.evidence_type: municipal hazard plan and operating context
records.empirical_evidence: The City hazard-mitigation plan identifies six flood types and reports 24 city pump stations with total design capacity of 50,891 cfs. It also records 69 significant flooding events in 1997–2019 using NOAA Storm Events data, while warning that some NOAA damage fields are unreliable.
records.validation_path: Pre-register one dated event and baseline, then compare eligible OPERA pixels with city pump/drainage records, NWS rainfall and river stages, and dated official street-flood reports where spatial precision is sufficient.
records.scope_limit: The historical event count is not a geocoded independent truth set, and the City notes limitations in the NOAA records; pump design capacity is not actual operating capacity during any event.

records.empirical_evidence: NYC DEP’s December 2025 report identifies 86 priority drainage areas in its 2024 Stormwater Analysis and reports 325 FloodNet sensors plus 241 sewer monitors citywide. The monitoring supports flood tracking and sewer performance work; agency counts are not local to the candidate box.
records.validation_path: Acquire dated FloodNet and NYC DEP records, independently review their spatial coverage against the 625 km² box, and validate a held-out event against municipal inundation or high-water labels rather than using capital-plan priority zones as truth.
records.scope_limit: The agency’s counts are citywide and do not imply that all sensors or priority areas fall within the candidate AOI.

records.empirical_evidence: California DWR describes more than 1,600 miles of State and federal levees in the Central Valley and more than 70 overtoppings or breaches since 1983; its flood-risk communication program sends notices to at-risk parcel owners across 17 counties.
records.validation_path: Use local Sacramento River/American River gauge and levee incident records, DWR floodplain layers, and event-date reference extents; exclude regional counts from the local denominator.
records.scope_limit: These metrics describe the broader Central Valley program, not the city-center AOI, and the cited page does not provide a local event-label dataset.

records.evidence_type: municipal watershed planning and event response
records.empirical_evidence: Atlanta Watershed Management publishes ten watershed improvement plans that identify infrastructure needs and recommended projects. City emergency communications also document active monitoring of road, drainage, and public-safety conditions during heavy-rain flooding; this is direct management relevance but not a quantified citywide loss series.
records.validation_path: Map plan project and stormwater geographies in the candidate box; evaluate a predeclared event using NWS rainfall, USGS stream gauges, and dated city incident/closure reports with location-level inclusion rules.
records.scope_limit: Plan coverage and agency response do not establish customer demand, parcel-level impacts, or independent event accuracy.

records.empirical_evidence: NWS reports that the Mississippi River at St. Louis crested at 49.58 ft on August 1, 1993, then a record, during the region’s Great Flood. This provides a strong riverine/floodwall stress context for an inland comparator.
records.validation_path: Use NOAA/NWS gauge records and recent dated event reports for actual validation; retain 1993 as contextual extreme-event history, not as a contemporaneous label for the 2024–2026 screen.
records.scope_limit: The headline evidence is historical and regional; it does not establish recent local flooding or current demand.

records.evidence_type: municipal flood-response capacity and multilateral research
records.empirical_evidence: DKI Jakarta reported 580 stationary pumps across 202 locations and 557 mobile pumps across its five administrative cities in 2024. The World Bank describes Greater Jakarta as a 14-municipality/district, three-province system facing recurring floods alongside water-supply and sanitation challenges, and calls for integrated urban-water management.
records.validation_path: Obtain dated BPBD flood-event and pump-operation records, rainfall and river/gate levels, then spatially resolve them to the fixed AOI. Engage local technical partners to review translation, data licensing, and location bias.
records.scope_limit: Pump counts are response-capacity inventory, not utilization or measured effectiveness; Greater Jakarta evidence spans well beyond the selected box.

records.evidence_type: national drainage performance and current risk context
records.empirical_evidence: PUB reports that flood-prone area fell from about 3,200 ha in the 1970s to less than 25 ha, a 99% reduction, while also identifying continuing flash-flood and coastal-flood risks and named hotspots. The historical reduction is a national management outcome, not an ATLAS result.
records.validation_path: Use PUB’s dated flood alerts, water-level sensor or rainfall records, and official hotspot polygons for a held-out event; spatially check each source against the common box and retain national statistics only as context.
records.scope_limit: National before/after flood-prone area figures cannot be attributed to the 625 km² screen or to satellite detection.

records.empirical_evidence: Dubai Municipality reports AED 1.439 billion in contracts across four Tasreef phases, more than 36 km of planned new drainage lines with contracts expected complete by 2027, and an estimated AED 30 billion total program cost. Its 700% discharge-capacity increase is a long-term design target over the next 100 years, not an observed performance result.
records.validation_path: Acquire municipality project alignments, construction status, rainfall, and dated incident/road-closure records; stratify completed and under-construction assets before any exposure analysis.
records.scope_limit: Published capacity values are future program targets and cannot serve as observed flood truth or current system performance.

records.empirical_evidence: India’s August 2026 UFRMP Phase I announcement includes Mumbai, with a city allocation of ₹707.71 crore and ₹150 crore reported released at that point. It documents funded implementation need; project completion and measured outcomes remain pending.
records.validation_path: Use BMC/Maharashtra dated rainfall, drainage works, pump/gauge operations, and geocoded flood incident records; separately identify pre- and post-project dates and verify data translation and spatial resolution.
records.scope_limit: Approval and release establish program activity, not completed works, reduced flooding, or customer demand.

records.empirical_evidence: World Bank urban-flood analysis describes Bangkok risk as the interaction of large upstream runoff, intense local rainfall, and tidal influence, with major flood-control works built following past floods. This makes the city a useful compound-driver comparator.
records.validation_path: Acquire Royal Irrigation Department and Bangkok Metropolitan Administration gauge, rainfall, pump, and event-closure records. Predefine local ground-truth sources and normalize Thai local time/date before matching satellite acquisitions.
records.scope_limit: The source is a planning/assessment report with historical context, not a current independent event label or an evaluation of ATLAS.

records.empirical_evidence: Tokyo Metropolitan Government reports that by October 2025 it had 30 operational storage basins across 14 rivers with about 2.73 million m³ capacity, plus about 12 km of diversion channels. It targets about 3.65 million m³ of total capacity by fiscal 2035 to address floods from rainfall above 50 mm/hour.
records.validation_path: Use Tokyo river/flood telemetry and rainfall with event reports and storage-facility service areas; assess source timestamps, datum and Japanese date/time conventions before event matching.
records.scope_limit: Capacity is metropolitan inventory/target, not proof of local flood absence or a satellite-classification accuracy measure.

records.empirical_evidence: The World Bank describes the Metro Manila Flood Management Project as covering 17 cities/municipalities and targeting more than one million people through pumping-station, drainage, solid-waste and control-system improvements.
records.validation_path: Obtain project pump and drainage locations, PAGASA rainfall, city/BWSC incident reports, and independently reviewed event extents. Resolve Metro Manila boundaries against the fixed city-center box and report only in-AOI evidence.
records.scope_limit: Project beneficiaries and footprint are regional targets, not actual affected persons or performance inside the candidate box.

records.evidence_type: municipal drainage plan and investment pipeline
records.empirical_evidence: São Paulo’s October 2026 drainage-plan release describes 201 interventions, 173 priority works, and a projected R$16.51 billion program through 2049. A separate municipal update reports 389 interventions completed since 2021; plan and commitment totals describe public management activity, not measured flood-loss reduction.
records.validation_path: Join dated municipal flood incident and rainfall records to geocoded interventions; separate completed/active/planned works, and validate a held-out event against independently reviewed high-water or flood-extent data.
records.scope_limit: Municipal project totals are citywide, may span the candidate box unevenly, and are not measured reduction in risk or proof of ATLAS demand.
